question: The Accelerated Female Literacy Programme was initiated in districts where the female literacy rate, based on the 2001 census, was ______:
solution:
The correct answer is __**below 30%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Accelerated Female Literacy Programme was initiated in districts where the female literacy rate was **below 30%** based on the 2001 census.
 
• This initiative aimed to address the significant gender gap in literacy rates.
 
• The program focused on **empowering women through education**, which is crucial for social and economic development.
 
• It included various measures such as adult education centers, literacy campaigns, and skill development programs to improve female literacy rates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Female Literacy Rate:**

 
 
• The female literacy rate is the percentage of women who can read and write at a specified age, typically 15 years and older.
 
• It is a crucial indicator of gender equality and women’s empowerment.
 
• Higher literacy rates among women are associated with better health outcomes, lower fertility rates, and improved economic opportunities.
 
 
 
• **2001 Census:**
 
 
• The 2001 Census of India was the 14th census conducted in the country.
 
• It provided comprehensive data on various demographic parameters, including literacy rates, population distribution, and socio-economic indicators.
 
• The data from the census is used for planning and implementing various government policies and programs.
 
 
 
• **Educational Initiatives for Women in India:**
 
 
• **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP):** Launched in 2015, this campaign aims to address the declining child sex ratio and promote the education and empowerment of girls.
 
• **Saakshar Bharat Mission:** Aimed at increasing adult literacy rates, particularly among women, by providing basic education and skill development.
 
• **National Programme for Education of Girls at Elementary Level (NPEGEL):** Focuses on enhancing the education of girls in educationally backward blocks.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Female Education:**
 
 
• Educated women are more likely to participate in the workforce, contributing to economic growth.
 
• They are better equipped to make informed decisions about health, nutrition, and family planning.
 
• Female education contributes to overall social development and reduces gender disparities.
